thread:
alex: Heads-up: proposing rollout plan for integrating FlashAttention v2/v3 into the runtime. Goals: kernel selection by shape, safe fallbacks, avoid KV-cache regressions, and clear telemetry.

maya: +1. Can you paste the kernel selection sketch and the feature-flag names you'll use?

alex: Kernel-picker sketch (pseudocode):
```
if ff_use_flashv3 and seq_len <= 2048 and head_dim in (64,128):
    kernel = flashv3
elif ff_use_flashv2 and seq_len <= 4096:
    kernel = flashv2
elif kv_mode == "paged":
    kernel = paged_attention
else:
    kernel = fused_attention
```
FFLAGS planned: ff_use_flashv2 (bool), ff_use_flashv3 (bool), ff_flash_priority ("v3"|"v2"|"fused").

jon: I ran a quick perf sweep on t4/g4 for llama-13B: seq buckets 64/512/2048. Summary: p50 tokens/sec: fused=1200, flashv2=1800, flashv3=1950. p95 latency: fused=42ms, v2=28ms, v3=25ms.
But saw ~9% regression on tiny-batch (batch 1-2) for v3 due to kernel-launch overhead.

maya: We should adapt batching heuristic: for small batches prefer fused until the batching window accumulates >= 30ms of waiting or batch_size>=4. Helps avoid worsened p95 on low-concurrency workloads.

sophia: KV cache note: v3 uses contiguous KV layout; paged-attn keeps pinned pages. For very long contexts (>32k tokens) v3 raises memory pressure and we observed eviction spikes. We should force paged fallback when kv_depth > 32k or when kv_page_faults trend up.

pat: Rollout plan proposal:
- Default: feature flags OFF.
- Alpha (internal): enable ff_use_flashv3 on 10% infra (canary), monitor tokens/sec, p95, OOMs.
- Beta: customer opt-in via console/ff.
- GA: flip on by default only for model profiles that meet perf gates.
Gating thresholds: tokens/sec >= +10% vs fused AND p95 <= -10% vs fused AND OOMs==0 during canary window.

alex: Telemetry we need: tags kernel=(flashv3|flashv2|fused), kv_mode=(contiguous|paged), seq_len_bucket=(128|512|2048|8192), batch_size_bucket. Also track kv_evictions/sec and kv_page_faults.

jon: Microbench snippet I ran:
```
model: llama-13b, batch=1, seq=64
fused: 120ms
v2: 78ms
v3: 84ms  <- overhead vs v2 for small seq
```
This is the small-batch sensitivity Maya mentioned.

maya: Also: sticky kernel per model/route for 5 minutes to avoid thrash when requests alternate shapes. We can store chosen kernel in per-route metadata and invalidate on model reload or config change.

sophia: For KV eviction/alerts: add metrics kv_evictions/sec and kv_page_fault_rate. Alert if kv_page_fault_rate > 0.1% of requests or kv_evictions/sec spikes 3x baseline. If triggered, runtime should set kv_mode=paged for affected routes.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: feature=ff_use_flashv3 scope=10% infra job=canary-1775129999 user=alex

alex: I'll open PR with: kernel chooser, feature flags, telemetry tags, and a benchmark harness. Assigning reviewers: @maya @jon.

maya: ack :thumbsup: please include a real-world trace (chatty short messages + long-context doc) in the bench set.

jon: posted bench script at bench/flash-picker-runner.sh. Note: reproducible GPU async stalls on cuda12.2 in our CI; need to verify on cuda12.3 and 13.x.

pat: I'll prepare rollback runbook and incident thresholds (OOM rate > 0.01% or p95 increase > 20%).

sophia: quick runtime tweak: expose env REDWOOD_KV_PAGE_SIZE and a guard to detect kv_depth at request start; if depth > 32768, force paged-mode for that request. I'll push a small patch.

alex: Good. Next sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to review canary metrics and decide on widening. Saving notes here for the rollout doc.

maya: thanks everyone.

jon: I'll follow up with raw perf logs and flamegraphs.

pat: adding oncall paging rule to the runbook.

sophia: dropping a short checklist in the PR: what to watch (tokens/sec, p95, kv_evictions, OOMs, model-routing thrash).

alex: thanks — end of thread.
